Puzzle 14 · 15 of 16

Not found, or no longer there?

Puzzles 11 and 13 showed that a class is loaded at its first use, by a loader searching the class path. Run the same small app three ways with a class missing, and learn what each error says about the cause.

Builds on: open one to see the idea this puzzle uses.

  • Puzzle 12: Why is it zero?

    A class's static code runs once, top to bottom, as one method the class file calls <clinit>. Any read of a static field whose line hasn't run yet silently sees the default value (0 or null), and if the static code throws, the class is marked as failed and every later use throws NoClassDefFoundError.

    Review puzzle 12

  • Puzzle 13: Why can't Greeter be cast to Greeter?

    A class loader finds class files and creates classes, but asks its parent first, up to the bootstrap loader, and defines a class itself only if no parent has it. While the program runs, a class is its name plus its defining loader, so two loaders that each define Greeter from the same file create two classes that can't be cast to each other.

    Review puzzle 13

The problem

An app ran fine on your machine. On a server it starts, serves requests for an hour, then crashes with NoClassDefFoundError. Another time it's ClassNotFoundException. Both sound like "class missing". Are they the same problem? And why didn't the JVM refuse to start if a class was missing all along?

See it

The building block

Run 1: a class deleted from the class path. App calls Helper.bonus(). Both were compiled together; then Helper.class was deleted, the way a jar can be left out of a deployment:

public class App {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        System.out.println("start");
        if (args.length > 0) {
            Class<?> k = Class.forName(args[0]);
            System.out.println("found " + k.getName());
            return;
        }
        System.out.println(Helper.bonus());
    }
}
$ java -cp out App
start
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Helper
	at App.main(App.java:9)
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Helper
	at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:641)
	at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.ClassLoaders$AppClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoaders.java:188)
	at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:526)
	... 1 more

start is printed: nothing needed Helper until line 9 (puzzle 11). There, the invokestatic for Helper.bonus must resolve the class, the application loader searches the class path, and finds nothing. The loader reports ClassNotFoundException; the JVM wraps it in NoClassDefFoundError, because compiled code depended on that class. Its documentation describes exactly this: the class "existed when the currently executing class was compiled, but the definition can no longer be found".

Run 2: a name in a string. Some code chooses classes at run time by name: plugin systems, serialization libraries, database drivers, dependency-injection libraries. They call Class.forName or a loader's loadClass with a string:

$ java -cp out App Missing
start
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Missing
	at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:641)
	...
	at java.base/java.lang.Class.forName(Class.java:414)
	at App.main(App.java:5)

No NoClassDefFoundError this time. ClassNotFoundException is an ordinary exception that methods like Class.forName declare, so the code that passed the name is expected to catch it and decide (try another driver, report a bad configuration). It says: "you asked for this name, and no loader had it".

ClassNotFoundExceptionNoClassDefFoundError
Who askedcode, with a name in a stringthe JVM, resolving a reference in compiled bytecode
What it meansthat name was never foundthe class was there at compile time and isn't usable now
Typical causewrong name, a driver or plugin not shippeda jar left out at run time, two library versions, or a failed static initializer (puzzle 12)
Who should handle itthe caller, which expected it might failusually nobody: fix the build or deployment

A NoClassDefFoundError with "Could not initialize class" is the other case from puzzle 12: the class was found, but its static initializer failed earlier. Read the message before reading the class path.

Run 3: the module path. Since JDK 9, Java code can be grouped into modules. A module is a named set of packages with a small file, module-info.java, that says what it needs and what it shares:

module app {
    requires bonus;
}

Modules are loaded from the module path, given with -p (or --module-path), instead of the class path. Same App and Helper, now in modules app and bonus, with the bonus module removed:

$ java -p mods -m app/dev.pachulski.app.App
Error occurred during initialization of boot layer
java.lang.module.FindException: Module bonus not found, required by app

start is not printed. Before running main, the JVM reads every requires line and checks each required module is there. A missing piece is found at startup, not an hour later at its first use. That is the module system's stated goal of "reliable configuration": the class path just lists files to search, so, in the module system's own design document's words, it's "impossible to tell, in advance, when an artifact is missing".

The edges

  • Many apps still use the class path. Anything started with -cp is, so the first-use behavior of run 1 is what you'll meet most often. Code on the class path belongs to the "unnamed module" and can still use the JDK's modules.
  • The first matching class wins. The class path is searched in order. Two jars containing different versions of the same class don't cause an error: the first one listed is used, and a method that exists only in the other version fails later with a different error, NoSuchMethodError. In a run with two folders holding Helper, version 1 listed first, Helper.bonus() returned version 1's answer and the call to a method only version 2 has failed with NoSuchMethodError: 'int Helper.extra()'. When a library behaves like an older version than you expected, list the class path and look for duplicates.
  • Fix the cause, not the catch. Catching NoClassDefFoundError hides a broken deployment. Catch ClassNotFoundException only where a name might legitimately be absent.

The analogy

Run 1 is a recipe book printed with "see page 40" on page 12, but page 40 was torn out. You only notice when you reach page 12, and the problem is the book, not you. Run 2 is a customer asking the clerk for a dish by name: the clerk says "we don't have that", and the customer is expected to pick something else. Run 3 is a kitchen that checks every ingredient on the list before opening: if one is missing, it doesn't open at all.

Run it yourself

javac -d out App.java Helper.java
rm out/Helper.class
java -cp out App
java -cp out App Missing
javac -d mods --module-source-path src -m app,bonus
java -p mods -m app/dev.pachulski.app.App

Before each java command, predict whether start is printed.

Check yourself

A server crashes with NoClassDefFoundError: com/example/Json, caused by ClassNotFoundException. The code calls Json.parse directly. What's the most likely cause?

Not quite. A direct call compiles to bytecode referring to Json; no string name is involved. Re-read that part ↑

Right. Compiled code depended on a class that isn't deployed.

Not quite. That message says "Could not initialize class" instead of being caused by ClassNotFoundException. Re-read that part ↑

The same app uses modules, and the module containing Json is missing. When does it fail?

Not quite. Required modules are checked before main runs.

Right. The module path checks requires lines first.

Not quite. Nothing substitutes a missing module; the JVM stops.

Your code loads a database driver with Class.forName(name). The driver isn't installed. What should the code expect?

Not quite. Class.forName throws; it never returns null for a missing class.

Not quite. A name in a string gives ClassNotFoundException, which the caller is expected to handle.

Right. Asking by name is expected to fail sometimes.

Sources
  • Java 21 API: NoClassDefFoundError ("Thrown if the Java Virtual Machine or a ClassLoader instance tries to load in the definition of a class (as part of a normal method call or as part of creating a new instance using the new expression) and no definition of the class could be found. The searched-for class definition existed when the currently executing class was compiled, but the definition can no longer be found.")
  • Java 21 API: ClassNotFoundException ("Thrown when an application tries to load in a class through its string name using: The forName method in class Class . The findSystemClass method in class ClassLoader . The loadClass method in class ClassLoader . but no definition for the class with the specified name could be found.")
  • The State of the Module System ("the specific goals of the module system are to provide Reliable configuration , to replace the brittle, error-prone class-path mechanism with a means for program components to declare explicit dependences upon one another"; "The module path is materially different from the class path, and more robust."; "This makes it impossible to tell, in advance, when an artifact is missing."; "If a request is made to load a type whose package is not defined in any known module then the module system will attempt to load it from the class path. If this succeeds then the type is considered to be a member of a special module known as the unnamed module")
  • JEP 261: Module System ("The module system constructs a module graph by resolving the transitive closure of the dependences of a set of root modules with respect to the set of observable modules.")
  • JEP 261: Module System also records "Release 9".
  • All three runs, and the two-version class path run, were produced in this session with OpenJDK 21.0.12.

What you now know

On the class path, a missing class is discovered only when code first needs it. ClassNotFoundException means code asked a loader for a name in a string and nothing was found; NoClassDefFoundError means compiled code referred to a class that can no longer be found or couldn't be initialized. On the module path, every required module is checked before main runs.
